title: Two collectors and the page share one private data repo and one rules record
builtFrom: index.html + js/github-db.js, collectors/cloud.md and pc.md, tools/ds.py and rules.json v1.9, as of Nov 21

nodes.name: PC-read sites
nodes.summary: Facebook Marketplace, Cycle Trader, eBay, nationwide Craigslist, Powder7
nodes.does: These sites block reads from the cloud, so only the PC collector reads them, in the Claude app's browser on Cameron's PC, signed in to Facebook with his own account. Facebook is swept from 11 US cities at 500 miles (skis: Denver, 150 miles); Cycle Trader by make and model; eBay newest first; Craigslist's nationwide searches from 8 US hubs (the cloud's reader can't open them); Powder7's used demo ski list.
rules: Browser conduct: read only; never type a password, message a seller or click anything that writes to an account
Facebook: at most 30 item pages and about 70 page loads per run
Never add sortBy to a Facebook search URL

nodes.name: Cloud-read sites
nodes.summary: Colorado Craigslist, Autotrader, PowerSports, MotoHunt, forums, SidelineSwap, Sports Plus
nodes.does: Sites whose pages load as text from the cloud. Craigslist here means the Colorado area pages for local-first searches; the nationwide Craigslist searches run on the PC. The cloud collector reads them with Claude's own web fetch: results pages first, then each matching ad. No paid scraper is used.
rules: A blocked site pauses: 24 h after one block, doubling with each block in a row, up to 7 days; ds.py sets the pause
Each site's pages are opened one at a time, never several at once
A site that only renders in a real browser moves to the PC (how: pc in sites.json)

nodes.name: Web search
nodes.does: Claude's web search fills in PC-only sites from search results between PC runs, finds listings on sites with no direct route, and researches which sites carry a new search's item (site plan). A search result never counts as a verified listing until the ad itself is opened.
rules: Snippets are stored as unverified and never make a site connected

nodes.name: Cameron
nodes.summary: Quick search, search editor, Searches tab (on or off, how often), paste box, listing status
nodes.does: Cameron adds or edits searches, pastes links from anywhere, and marks listings watching, contacted or passed. The page saves each of these straight to the data repo with his GitHub token. Each search has a kind (Vehicle, Skis or Something else), picked in the quick box or the editor, and the kind decides which fields the editor shows. The editor's limits decide which listings belong in the search, on every device: year range, max miles, price ceiling and ship rule, and for skis the wanted models, length, underfoot and bindings. On the Searches tab he turns each search on or off and picks how often it runs (every day, every 2 or 3 days, once a week); turning one on starts it at the next collector run, and a search that is off keeps its listings but nothing is read, refreshed, checked or emailed for it.
nodes.code: index.html: parseQuick(), parseSkiQuick(), guessKind(), openEditor(), renderKindFields(), parseLine(), status select in renderList(), renderSearches(), setSearchOn(), setSearchEvery()
rules: The page writes only its own files: searches.json, pasted.json, status.json
A search's own limits come before the sidebar filters, which only narrow inside them
A search's kind comes from rules.json kinds; a free-form filter builder was left out on purpose, since every filter needs collector instructions
Collectors never change a search's on/off switch or frequency (active, everyDays, activeSince); ds.py refuses

nodes.name: Cloud collector
nodes.summary: Fires 12:06 and 6:06 am/pm MT and works only the searches that are on and due (an every-day search runs at 6:06 pm), Opus 5.5, web fetch and web search, never emails
nodes.does: A scheduled task that clones both repos, reads rules.json, and works out which searches are due this run (on, and due by how often Cameron set them to run; ds due). It does nothing for the rest, and a run with nothing due stops right away. For each due search it reads every cloud site, opening refused pages through a web-search result first and flagging a site for the PC after 3 refused runs; sets up quick searches, site plans and what-to-verify notes; reads each ad (check 1); marks deal-priced ads "Waiting for the PC photo check"; refreshes prices; writes its own cloud route on each site it read and one run record per due search; pushes through ds.py. Pasted links are read whatever their search's schedule.
nodes.code: collectors/cloud.md (scheduled task 'Deal Scout: cloud collector' just points to it)
rules: All sections of rules.json
Never reviews photos and never emails: the PC does both
Records ski specs (brand, model, length, underfoot, bindings) on every ski listing and looks up maker underfoot specs, at most 10 a run
Works only searches that are on and due this run (rules.json SCHEDULE)

nodes.name: PC collector
nodes.summary: Once daily at 8:36 pm MT (after the cloud run), searches that are on and due, Opus 5.5, Claude app browser on the PC, sends deal emails
nodes.does: A scheduled task that runs with Cameron's PC linked, for the searches that are on and due this run (ds due); a run with nothing due stops right away. Reads Facebook, Cycle Trader, eBay, the nationwide Craigslist searches and Powder7 in the Claude app's browser; reviews the photos of every deal-priced ad from any site, biggest discount first, up to 8 a run (settled caution verdicts wait for a price change or 7 days) by opening each image and taking a screenshot (needs the Claude window visible; otherwise the check waits); runs the independent second look for exceptional deals; confirms price and availability on the ad; then sends the deal email. Writes its own pc route and run records. A run with the PC offline is marked skipped, so its searches stay due for the next run.
nodes.code: collectors/pc.md (scheduled task 'Deal Scout: PC collector' just points to it)
rules: Photo checks happen only here (rules.json: LEGITIMACY CHECK)
A blank screenshot leaves the check pending; never passed
Records ski specs (brand, model, length, underfoot, bindings) on every ski listing and looks up maker underfoot specs, at most 10 a run
Named ski models are searched by name; Facebook gets at most 3 a run
Works only searches that are on and due this run (rules.json SCHEDULE); no photo checks or deal emails for the others

nodes.name: Rules (rules.json)
nodes.summary: One record both collectors and the page follow
nodes.does: Deal Scout's shared rules: thresholds and windows in numbers, the rule wording the collectors follow in text, the Checks tab cards in display, and the item kinds (Vehicle, Skis, Something else) in kinds. A kind lists the fields collectors record for it, the sidebar filters and search limits it offers, its pricing default, and for skis the word lists used to read brand, model, length, underfoot and bindings from titles. The schedule block sets when a search day starts (5 pm Denver time), the frequency choices and each collector's run times, which the page uses to show each search's next run. Change a rule once here and every part picks it up on its next run or page load.
rules: Edited only in a build chat, then one test run of each collector
photoBackup is "off": no paid photo service, and helper agents get the same rule
Skis: pickup listings rank ahead of ship-in at the same deal state, and ship-in skis with no shipping shown are priced with a $40 estimate

nodes.name: ds.py data helper
nodes.summary: How collectors read and change the data
nodes.does: A small Python script the collectors run for every read and write: summaries, which searches are due this run (worked out once at the start and kept for the run; no queue work, scores or run records for the others), scoring (the same logic as the page), the work queues (which listings to re-open this run and which need a photo check, in order), storing listings, checks, routes and runs. It records each change, and on push it replays them on the newest copy if the other collector pushed first, so nothing gets overwritten; a change that no longer applies is skipped and reported, and a replay cut off partway is redone on the next push. It also sets a blocked site's pause from the rules record. For ski searches it reads brand, model, length, underfoot and bindings from each listing's title and notes into specs, never overwriting what a collector sent, and `ds.py specs` backfills stored listings.
rules: Collectors never hand-edit JSON or force-push
Each collector may write only its own route on a site
A route can name the searches its read covered; the page judges a site per search
Works out which listings are probably gone (unseen 7 days while the site read fine) the same way the page does
Leaves listings outside a search's limits out of deals, the median and the refresh queue, the same way the page does
Applies ski length, underfoot, binding and named-model limits the same way the page does; an unknown value never puts a listing outside
Adds the $40 shipping estimate and the pickup-first order to scoring and the photo queue, the same way the page does
Works out which searches are due the same way the page shows the next run, and notes on each route which due searches the read covered

nodes.name: Data repo (dealscout-data)
nodes.summary: Private GitHub repo of JSON files
nodes.does: The only shared state, as plain files with full history: searches.json, listings/<search>.json, sites.json (each with a cloud and a pc route), runs.json, rules.json, settings.json, plus status.json and pasted.json from the page. Every collector run is a commit you can read.
rules: Listing ids are <site>-<site listing id>, which is how duplicates are caught
status.json and pasted.json are written by the page only

nodes.name: Deal email
nodes.summary: Checked deals only, from the PC collector
nodes.does: One email per run listing new deals that passed every required check, with what the check covered and a link to the ad and the page. Sent from the Gmail connector's account to settings.json dealEmailTo, where Cameron's own Gmail filter files it out of the inbox; the sending account's Sent copy goes to Trash right after. Site problems are never emailed; they show as the banner on the page.
nodes.code: Gmail connector (send_message, then get_message + trash_message on the Sent copy); rules.json DEAL EMAILS
rules: Re-open every ad right before sending; drop anything gone or changed
Never email a site problem
Trash only the Sent copy of the email just sent, never anything else

nodes.name: Deal Scout page
nodes.summary: GitHub Pages site, your token per device
nodes.does: The page at cbelknap980.github.io/DealScout. It reads the data repo with Cameron's GitHub token, re-checks every minute while open, and re-scores every listing in the browser with the rules record. It opens on Listings: checked deals as photo cards on top, then every listing with filters for deal state, price, distance, how you'd get it (pickup or ships), site, status and price drops, plus the search kind's own filters: year and miles for vehicles; brand, length, underfoot, binding type and brand, and women's for skis. Each row has Watch, Contacted and Pass. Searches lists every search with an on/off switch, how often it runs, and when it last ran and runs next; searches that are off are greyed out on Listings too. Sites, Checks and this diagram are the other tabs; Sites judges each site per search, from the routes that covered that search. A listing unseen for 7 days while its site read fine counts as probably gone and moves under Gone. A listing outside the search's own limits from Edit search (years, max miles, price ceiling, far away and not shipping when the search asks for that, or for skis a model, length, underfoot or binding it rules out) never counts as a deal and moves under Outside search unless you marked it; the filters only narrow inside those limits. In ski searches, pickup listings sort ahead of ship-in ones in Best deal, and ship-in skis with no shipping shown carry a $40 estimate in their price.
nodes.code: index.html (score(), itemOutside(), specOutside(), siteStatus(), renderListings(), passes(), kindGroups(), specGroup(), renderResults(), renderSearches(), nextRun(), renderSites(), renderChecks()); js/github-db.js (data layer)
rules: The token stays in the browser on each device; it can only reach dealscout-data
Search limits leave a listing out of the open list and deals; years and miles also keep it out of the median
Ski filters treat a value the ad doesn't state as its own choice (Not stated or Include ones with no length listed), never as a mismatch
A search that runs every few days keeps its prices fresh and its sites connected until its next run (windows grow by the days between runs)
